questions.question: In a reactive client application, what is the primary consequence of mutating state directly instead of using dispatch or setter hooks?
options: Component reconciliation fails to trigger re-renders, causing stale UI bugs
The JavaScript runtime crashes with an out-of-memory error
The backend API connection is immediately aborted
The browser layout engine forces synchronous reflow on every thread
questions.explanation: React checks shallow references. Mutating state in-place keeps the memory reference identical, bypassing reconciliation.

questions.question: Which SQL constraint ensures that rows in a child table cannot reference a non-existent record in the parent table?
options: FOREIGN KEY constraint with referential integrity
UNIQUE INDEX constraint
CHECK constraint on scalar values
AUTO_INCREMENT sequence lock
questions.explanation: Foreign keys enforce referential integrity between matching parent-child relational entities.

questions.question: Where should short-lived JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for authentication be stored on mobile native clients to prevent unauthorized extraction?
options: Hardware-backed secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android KeyStore)
Unencrypted AsyncStorage or LocalStorage files
In a public static environment variable file
In the plain app bundle manifest
questions.explanation: Hardware keychains provide cryptographic isolation preventing sandboxed file access.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of running automated linting and unit test suites on every pull request prior to merging?
options: Early detection of regression defects before code hits staging/production branches
Eliminating the requirement for backend database indexes
Reducing the physical size of the server operating system image
Accelerating network round-trip latency to edge CDNs
questions.explanation: Shift-left verification ensures regression bugs never pollute trunk branches.

questions.question: In an engineering production environment, what is the primary purpose of defining Service Level Objectives (SLOs)?
options: Setting target reliability and performance metrics aligned with user satisfaction
Maximizing developer shift hours during non-incident cycles
Completely eliminating all cloud infrastructure spend
Replacing the need for structured logging and trace events
questions.explanation: SLOs specify target boundaries (e.g. 99.9% uptime) that govern development velocity vs reliability.

questions.question: When designing an idempotent payment creation endpoint, how do you prevent double-billing if a network timeout occurs mid-request?
options: Require a unique Idempotency-Key header and cache transaction state in a fast distributed store
Automatically issue a refund on every 504 Gateway Timeout error
Retry the exact same unflagged request five times in a tight loop
Disable transaction isolation levels in the relational database
questions.explanation: Idempotency keys ensure server-side deduplication regardless of network client retries.

questions.question: In an asynchronous Node.js microservice handling 10,000 req/sec, what happens if a synchronous CPU-heavy loop is executed in an API route?
options: The single event loop thread is blocked, freezing all concurrent requests across the instance
Node.js spawns 1,000 separate operating system processes automatically
Traffic is instantly rerouted to GPU workers without latency degradation
Only the calling client experiences delays while others remain sub-10ms
questions.explanation: Node.js runs on a single event loop thread. Synchronous CPU tasks freeze handling of concurrent I/O.

questions.question: What is the primary architectural tradeoff when adding multiple composite indexes to a high-write relational database table?
options: Faster SELECT query execution times at the expense of slower INSERT/UPDATE throughput and increased disk footprint
Decreased disk usage but higher latency on indexed read queries
Automatic conversion of all B-tree indexes into volatile RAM hashes
Total prevention of database deadlocks during batch operations
questions.explanation: Every write requires updating index trees on disk, degrading write throughput while speeding up reads.

questions.question: When an external microservice experiences intermittent 503 service unavailable errors, which design pattern prevents catastrophic thundering herds?
options: Exponential backoff retry with randomized jitter and circuit breaking
Immediate aggressive infinite polling without sleep intervals
Dropping all incoming consumer events permanently without an audit log
Crashing the container worker pod immediately
questions.explanation: Exponential backoff spread with jitter de-synchronizes retry spikes, preventing self-inflicted DDoS.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using discriminated unions with a literal discriminator key over generic 'any' typing?
questions.snippet: type Action = { type: 'SUCCESS'; payload: Data } | { type: 'ERROR'; error: string };
options: Enables exhaustive compile-time narrowing and prevents accessing missing properties
Speeds up browser JavaScript runtime compilation speed by 40%
Eliminates the requirement for unit tests in downstream codebases
Allows arbitrary dynamic key assignment without compiler complaints
questions.explanation: Discriminated unions force type safety across branch checks at compile time.

questions.question: In distributed microservices, what mechanism allows tracing a single customer transaction across 6 distinct downstream service hops?
options: Propagating a unique Correlation / Trace ID via HTTP headers across all service boundaries
Logging the physical MAC address of the host database server
Recording the client timestamp without timezone normalization
Using synchronous database transactions across multiple clouds
questions.explanation: Correlation IDs (W3C Trace Context) connect disparate log events into a unified distributed trace.

questions.question: Under high read concurrency, what failure mode occurs when a heavily queried cache key expires simultaneously, and how is it mitigated?
options: Cache Stampede (Thundering Herd); mitigated via mutual exclusion distributed locks or probabilistic early expiration (XFetch)
Memory Fragmentation; mitigated by disabling cache eviction policies
Split-Brain Condition; mitigated by disabling database replication
Cascading Deadlock; mitigated by switching cache protocols from TCP to UDP
questions.explanation: Cache Stampedes overwhelm databases when hundreds of queries miss simultaneously upon TTL expiration.

questions.question: Which transaction isolation level prevents phantom reads and serialization anomalies at the cost of potential serialization failure aborts?
options: SERIALIZABLE
READ COMMITTED
READ UNCOMMITTED
REPEATABLE READ without predicate locks
questions.explanation: Serializable isolation guarantees that concurrent transaction outcomes are identical to serial execution.

questions.question: In event-driven architectures, how is dual-write inconsistency avoided when simultaneously saving a local database entity and publishing a message to a broker?
options: Transactional Outbox Pattern with an asynchronous CDC / log tailing publisher
Running the database write and broker publish in an uncoordinated Promise.all()
Publishing to the message broker first and rolling back on database failure
Using HTTP webhooks instead of a persistent broker
questions.explanation: The Outbox pattern writes domain changes and outgoing events in the same atomic database transaction.

questions.question: According to the CAP Theorem, when an unavoidable network partition occurs in a distributed data cluster, what fundamental tradeoff must be made?
options: Choose between Consistency (returning latest data or erroring) and Availability (returning stale data without error)
Choose between Partition Tolerance and Total Disk Encryption
Sacrifice both Latency and Security to maintain full CPU concurrency
Guarantee 100% throughput across all regions simultaneously without replication lag
questions.explanation: During partitions (P), distributed systems can prioritize immediate consistency (CP) or constant response availability (AP).

questions.question: What is the primary indicator that an engineering deliverable is ready for production deployment?
options: Passing all automated integration tests, meeting performance baselines, and passing security audits
The project builds successfully on one developer's local workstation
Code comments have been removed to reduce bundle file sizes
Database migrations are performed manually directly on the production instance
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires verified automated regression passes and security compliance.

questions.question: When refactoring a legacy operational pipeline, what is the best practice to avoid breaking critical downstream dependents?
options: Maintain backward-compatible API contracts and deploy behind feature flags with canary rollout
Rename public schema fields immediately to reflect newer terminology
Shut down the older service version completely during business hours
Disable integration telemetry until the refactor is 100% finalized
questions.explanation: Contract versioning and feature flags ensure non-breaking transitions for downstream consumers.

questions.question: How do technical organizations prevent silent data corruption in mission-critical distributed storage pipelines?
options: End-to-end cryptographic checksum verification (SHA-256) and periodic reconciliation audits
Relying solely on local operating system file permissions
Assuming transport layer TCP checksums catch 100% of bit-rot defects
Increasing server memory without adding data validation layers
questions.explanation: Cryptographic checksums detect storage media bit-rot, transmission corruption, and software bugs.
